transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-04-14 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Liam (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Alex (NimbleDocs CTO), Sofia (Eng Mgr), Daniel (Privacy), Priya (Product)

Summary: Quick discovery and fit-check for Redwood self-serve path; emphasis on time-to-first-token, free credits, and security/priv constraints for a potential pilot. We touched hosted vs dedicated vs VPC/private for PII workflows and agreed to run a short benchmark and exchange security docs.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Liam (Redwood): Okay, everyone can hear me? Great. Thanks for joining, we appreciate the time. Quick intros? I'll keep it fast. I'm Liam, AE on the account. Priya's our solutions engineer, she'll jump into latency/cost stuff.
[00:18] Alex (NimbleDocs): Hi all, Alex here, CTO at NimbleDocs. We build a doc ingestion and question answering product for legal teams, lots of PII so privacy is huge.
[00:28] Sofia (NimbleDocs): Sofia, engineering manager, mostly rolling this out with Alex.
[00:33] Daniel (NimbleDocs): Daniel, privacy lead. I'm mainly here to vet compliance and KMS details.
[00:38] Liam: Awesome. Goal for today: make sure self-serve/PLG path will let you get to a prototype quickly (time-to-first-token), give you an idea of hosted vs Dedicated vs Private fit, and capture the constraints for a pilot. Also we can allocate some free credits.
[00:55] Priya (Redwood): I'll cover the perf side and what our quickstart looks like — e.g., typical token credit sizes, sequence lengths, and how KV cache helps for long-doc QA.
[01:08] Alex: Cool. First Q — how fast can we get something running? We want to spin up a prototype in a week ideally.
[01:16] Liam: With self-serve you can sign up and do first calls in under an hour; with our quickstart we give credits so you can actually hit endpoints. Time-to-first-token is usually minutes after sign-up if you have prompts ready.
[01:27] Sofia: Are there any hoops for company accounts? SSO?
[01:31] Liam: For self-serve you can use email, but we can convert to an org with SSO/SAML, RBAC and invite your team. For the pilot we usually do a trial org and add credits — no contract needed for initial testing.
[01:45] Daniel: Ok, privacy: our legal team requires data at rest encryption with customer-managed keys, and retention controls. Do you offer KMS integrations?
[01:54] Priya: Yes, for Private deployments we support KMS/HSM and customer-managed keys. For Hosted we have encryption at rest; we also offer Bring-Your-Own-Key for Redwood Dedicated in some contracts — we'll share the exact flow.
[02:07] Alex: Important — some of our documents must never leave our VPC, we may need on-prem or VPC peering.
[02:13] Liam: That's a common ask. Quick mapping: Hosted API = fastest, PLG-friendly. Dedicated = reserved GPU pools with isolation and SLA. Private = VPC or on-prem package for strict residency. For PII, many customers start on Dedicated or Private. But you can prototype on Hosted with proper NDAs and then move.
[02:35] Sofia: Cost question — if we start on Hosted for prototype, will the unit costs be significantly higher than Dedicated?
[02:41] Priya: Usually Hosted unit cost is higher at scale due to shared infra. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower per-token when you commit capacity. But for quick prototyping Hosted is typically fine — especially if we enable intelligent caching and batching which reduces tokens.
[02:55] Alex: You mentioned KV cache; is that automatic?
[02:59] Priya: We have automatic prefix/KV caching for repeated contexts — it helps a lot for doc-based QA where the same doc pieces get re-used. It's turned on by default for certain routes, and you can configure TTLs. It's part of Redwood Optimize recommendations too.
[03:16] [03:18] Alex: Got it. For the trial, we'll need to run a throughput test with real docs. Can Redwood run benchmarks or do we run them?
[03:25] Priya: We can run them together. Typical flow: you share a representative prompt set and doc samples, we run latency and token cost runs against hosted and a Dedicated-equivalent profile so you get real numbers. We'll also show how batching and quantization change numbers.
[03:41] Daniel: On the compliance docs — can you share SOC2 and ISO? Also audit logs are a must.
[03:47] Liam: Absolutely. We'll send SOC 2, ISO attestation, and our audit logging docs. For Hosted we provide request-level audit logs; for Dedicated and Private you get more granular control and retention policies.
[03:59] Sofia: Any red flags we've seen when customers try to move from hosted prototype to dedicated? Time and ops complexity?
[04:07] Priya: There's a small ramp — Dedicated requires capacity planning (commits), autoscaling rules, and potentially network setup. We'll support with a runbook and rollback policies. Many teams do a staged pilot: prototype on Hosted, run a benchmark, then spin up Dedicated for a short committed window.
[04:25] Alex: What's the shortest Dedicated trial you've seen?
[04:29] Liam: Some customers do a one-month reserved pilot or pilot with burst capacity. We can be flexible. For your use-case with PII, I'd recommend an initial dedicated pilot or Private if your legal team is strict.
[04:42] Priya: Also worth noting, you can pin model versions to avoid regressions. We also have eval hooks.
[04:49] [05:00] Alex: Regarding models — do you host open models only or do you also federate access to proprietary models?
[05:04] Priya: Our model catalog includes curated open models and Redwood-verified profiles. For enterprise customers we can bring private weights into Dedicated/Private deployments under NDA, yes.
[05:12] Sofia: Good. Now, on the technical side: our typical sequence lengths are long — average 1.5k tokens with some 6k. Will that affect latency?
[05:24] Priya: Sequence length definitely impacts latency. Our runtime does kernel selection and attention optimizations; for long sequences we recommend models with efficient attention and we can suggest quantization profiles. We'll show a perf matrix in the benchmark.
[05:38] Daniel: Any differences in logging or PII masking between Hosted and Dedicated?
[05:44] Liam: Hosted has default redaction options and token-level cost breakdowns; Dedicated/Private can be configured to scrub or not log inputs depending on your retention policy.
[05:55] Alex: Is there a way to limit model outputs to remove sensitive data? Some of our use cases need hallucination guardrails.
[06:03] Priya: Yes— we support response filters, deterministic sampling knobs, and you can put post-processing webhooks. We also have function/tool calling to enforce structured outputs which reduces hallucination surface.
[06:18] [06:30] Sofia: For time-to-first-token, do you provide SDKs and examples?
[06:34] Liam: We have SDKs in Python, Node, and Go, plus quickstart curl examples. We'll share a repo link. Typical developer flow is sign-up -> get API key -> run sample prompt.
[06:45] Alex: Can we invite a couple of our engineers to the org so they can play with keys?
[06:49] Liam: Yes, the trial org supports invites, RBAC can be set later.
[06:53] Daniel: About network setup — if we move to Private, how quick is provision?
[06:59] Priya: For VPC deployments it's usually a few weeks for networking and compliance steps. On-prem can take longer depending on your infra team. We have a standard checklist.
[07:10] Alex: I want to understand real numbers. Can we look at an example token cost and latency for a 1k token call on hosted vs dedicated?
[07:18] Priya: Roughly on hosted you'll see higher per-token; on Dedicated commit profiles the cost per token can be 20-40% lower depending on volume. For latency, Dedicated with reserved GPU pools gives more consistent tail latency and throughput. We'll include a cost/latency slide in the benchmark doc.
[07:35] Sofia: For the trial credits, how granular are they? Do we get token buckets or $ credits?
[07:41] Liam: We usually provision token credits and track per-route token usage. We can also create test keys and expire them.
[07:48] [08:00] Alex: Ok, let's talk about pilot success criteria. For us it's: 1) 95th percentile latency under 750ms for short queries, 2) cost per query under $0.02 for average QA session, 3) compliance gating for PII.
[08:15] Priya: Those are reasonable. We'll validate 95p latency during the benchmark and show cost projections for expected traffic.
[08:24] Daniel: For KMS, our vendor is HashiCorp Vault. Is that supported?
[08:29] Liam: We integrate with common KMS providers; HashiCorp Vault is supported in Dedicated/Private deployments — we'll send the integration notes.
[08:38] Sofia: Any limitations with streaming responses and function calls in hosted mode?
[08:43] Priya: Streaming and function/tool calling are supported in Hosted; function calling is the same across modes. For very low-latency streaming you might prefer Dedicated to reduce variability.
[08:56] Alex: If we wanted to test a private model weight, is that part of the pilot?
[09:01] Priya: We can load private weights into Dedicated/Private under NDA. For quick prototyping you can also containerize inference and use the hosted API as an adapter.
[09:12] [09:30] Alex: Great. Can you walk through the quickstart steps so my team can start today?
[09:35] Liam: Sure — Step 1: I'll provision a trial org and seed 50k token credits. Step 2: We'll send a quickstart guide and SDK repo link. Step 3: You send sample prompts/docs to Priya. Step 4: we'll run a shared benchmark and iterate. Should take you to first token in under an hour if you follow the quickstart.
[09:56] Sofia: That sounds good. How will we share sample data securely? We prefer a temporary S3 bucket or a transfer link.
[10:03] Liam: S3 link with short expiry is fine. We'll add instructions for redaction before upload.
[10:10] Daniel: Are there any default data retention periods? We need to set retention to 30 days max for trial.
[10:16] Priya: We can set retention rules for your trial org, yes. Default hosted retention is configurable per org, we'll show where to change it.
[10:27] Alex: On billing — if we go beyond credits, how's invoicing handled?
[10:31] Liam: After credits, usage-based billing kicks in. For Dedicated/Private we do reserved contracts with monthly invoices. We'll share pricing tiers.
[10:39] Sofia: I want to flag that our legal team will require a DPA and a data flow diagram.
[10:45] Liam: We'll provide a DPA template and example data flow diagrams — send your legal contact and we'll loop them in.
[10:52] Daniel: What about support levels for the pilot — is there an on-call SE?
[10:56] Priya: For pilots the SE is available during business hours; for Dedicated you can opt for a support SLA. We'll propose an on-call window for the benchmark week.
[11:08] [11:30] Alex: Any known gotchas with long doc contexts and token usage spiking?
[11:36] Priya: If you naively send whole documents each time tokens can spike. Suggestions: chunking, embeddings + retrieval, caching prefixes, or vector store + reranking to reduce token counts. We'll include a best-practices doc.
[11:52] Liam: Also our Optimize tool suggests batching and quantization per workload which often halves cost in production.
[12:00] Sofia: For the benchmarking, can we have a quick list of metrics you'll provide?
[12:05] Priya: Sure: latency p50/p90/p95, tokens per request, cost per 1k tokens estimate, throughput (requests/s), memory/GPU utilization for the model, and accuracy/regression metrics on a prompt set.
[12:20] Alex: Sounds thorough. If you could include an A/B between open model v a tuned private weight that'd be ideal.
[12:27] Priya: We can do that.
[12:30] [12:45] Daniel: One more on security — do you persist model inputs on hosted by default? 
[12:49] Liam: By default we log minimal metadata; storing raw inputs is opt-in and configurable. For trials we can disable raw input persistence.
[12:58] Sofia: Great. Any latency SLO for hosted API?
[13:02] Priya: We don't SLA free hosted accounts, but we do publish performance profiles. Dedicated comes with latency SLOs in contracts.
[13:12] Alex: Ok let's confirm immediate next steps and owners before we wrap.
[13:17] Liam: I'll summarize: 1) Liam will provision trial org and seed 50k tokens; 2) Priya will run benchmark once sample data is uploaded; 3) Alex team to share prompts and docs; 4) Daniel will send KMS and compliance constraints. We'll send SOC2/ISO and DPA.
[13:33] Alex: Agreed. Also please include links to SDK and quickstart repo.
[13:37] Liam: Yes — I'll share links and the trial invite. Links we'll send: quickstart repo (https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickstart), security pack (https://redwood.example.com/security-pack.pdf), pilot runbook (https://redwood.example.com/pilot-runbook).
[13:53] Priya: For the benchmark, please include: typical prompt distribution, sample docs, and expected QPS. We'll schedule a 1-hour session to run tests.
[14:02] Daniel: Can we have that session next Thursday morning?
[14:06] Priya: I have availability next Thursday 09:00-11:00 PT, otherwise Friday morning.
[14:13] Alex: Thursday 09 PT works for us.
[14:17] Liam: Great — we'll send a calendar invite.
[14:20] Sofia: Any final questions?
[14:23] Alex: None from me. Thanks.
[14:25] Daniel: No. Thanks for the clarity.
[14:27] Liam: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with those artifacts and the trial.
[14:30] [End of recording — call ended after wrap-up and some quick side chat about SAML setup for their org]
